q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a refrigerator?
title: Refrigerator carbon footprint per unit
short: Add the steel cabinet, plastic liner, insulation foam, compressor and copper tubing per unit with supplier figures, then add the plant's energy per unit built. Count the refrigerant as its own line: HFCs warm strongly if they leak, while hydrocarbons such as R600a barely do.

ul: Pre-painted steel sheet for the cabinet and doors.
Plastic inner liner, shelves and door liners.
Compressor, condenser, copper and aluminium tubing.
Foaming the cabinet with polyurethane insulation.
Refrigerant charging, leak testing and assembly.

p: Report per refrigerator by type and capacity in litres, and state the refrigerant and its charge in grams, taken from the rating plate.

example.title: Worked example: refrigerator unit per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 162,500 / 12,000 = 13.5 kg CO2 per unit
Add steel, plastics, compressor, foam and refrigerant for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
